title: Higher-resolution art, and Jan drawing in Pixel Forge
started_from: Emerson: "o mroe and more make it lookk better higehr res pixel textures ad also make a jan able to make sprits and structure in pixel forge"
intended: Two things: make Janhollow look better with higher-resolution pixel textures, and give Pixel Forge a way to have Jan make sprites and structures.

the_art.what_changed: The station was drawn with 16px crewroom tiles, where a metal floor is four pixels of detail. It now renders at 32px from a generated janhollow-deck pack: floor plates with panel seams, bolts and wear, corridor grating, a lit strip down the middle of a run, soil for the garden deck, a two-panel door with a light over it, a lift pad with chevrons, and a sixteen-variant autotile wall set.
the_art.how_the_crew_kept_up: Mixing 16px characters with 32px tiles is the thing that actually looks wrong. Rather than redraw eight anime crew, they are upscaled with EPX (Scale2x), the pixel-art doubling rule that rounds a diagonal instead of turning one pixel into a 2x2 block. The crewroom props go through the same pass. Everything on screen is now native 32px.
the_art.autotiling: A wall picks one of wall_0..wall_15 from which of its four sides have another wall beside them, so a corner is drawn as a corner and a face onto a room gets a bright lip. Nothing in the data says where a corner is; it falls out of the map.
the_art.lighting: One dark overlay per deck with light punched out of it at lamps, consoles, reactors, viewports, doors and the lift, then a warm or cold glow added back on top of each. Rebuilt only when the deck or the view changes. Tuned by eye against screenshots: the first version at 0.62 opacity was so dark the new texture was invisible, which defeated the point of drawing it.
the_art.two_atlases: Tiles bake against the new janhollow palette and the crew against the crewroom one, so the deck can be re-skinned (night shift, red alert) without touching a character. Sprites are asked for by qualified pack/name because the 32px packs deliberately reuse the 16px names.
the_art.still_data: Deck files name their floor sprite and palette; rooms may override the floor, which is how the garden decks got soil and the engineering rooms got worn plate. Adding a tile is still one entry in tools/make_art32.py, and everything it writes is editable in Pixel Forge.

jan_in_pixel_forge.the_finding_that_shaped_it: Local models cannot draw pixels. Measured on 2026-09-16: asked for a 16x16 grid of palette characters, the 4B returned sixteen rows of pure transparency — an empty image — and the 9B returned rows of 16, 17 and 18 characters with scattered diagonal noise. Asked instead for a short list of shapes, both models produced sensible, well-formed parts first time. So the model composes and the code draws.
jan_in_pixel_forge.what_was_built: apps/pixelforge/janart.py: the two prompts, a parser that repairs what these models actually get wrong (hex codes in the colour field, fenced code blocks, a legend where a palette was asked for, coordinates off the canvas, trailing commas), a rasteriser for rect, ellipse, line and pixel, and a guard that refuses an empty, single-colour or runaway drawing.
jan_in_pixel_forge.structures: The same shape list at tile scale is a floor plan: each key is a tile id from the library rather than a colour, and the tile list offered to the model is read from the library so a tile drawn today is offered tomorrow. Saved as shared content under the new 'structures' type in forge_content, where any game can read it.
jan_in_pixel_forge.what_it_actually_produces: A red toolbox at 16x16 in 66 s: recognisable, two colours, crude. A 12x9 crew cabin in 82 s: a wall border, a wood floor, a rug, a bed and a door in the wall — genuinely usable. Floor plans are where this earns its keep; sprites are a sketching aid.

shared_work: shared/forge_jan.py gained chat(): one Jan request, thinking off by default, serialised through a process-wide lane. Every Forge app that talks to Jan now gets the thinking-off default, which the measurements in session 2 showed is not optional. janhollow/janclient.py was rewired to use it and lost its duplicate HTTP code.
shared/forge_content.py gained the 'structures' type — one registry entry, because a hut is a hut whichever game stamps it.
verified: apps/janhollow tests → 57 pass (8 new: EPX doubling and diagonal rounding, transparency, every autotile variant present and correctly lit, the generator being deterministic, and the packs on disk validating against the palette with no stray colours).
apps/pixelforge tests → 15 pass, all without Jan: every malformed reply in them is one a model actually sent.
apps/emberfield → 123 pass, and tests/test_forge_jan.py → 6 pass, against both shared changes.
Live through the real 4B: a sprite and two floor plans, end to end through the HTTP API, including one saved and reloaded into the page.
Screenshots looked at: the habitat deck and the garden deck at 32px, and the Ask Jan panel showing a generated cabin rendered with real tile sprites.
black and pyright clean on everything touched.
got_wrong_and_fixed: The first lighting pass was far too dark: the new texture was invisible. Opacity down from 0.62 to 0.38, ambient reworked, and a warm additive glow added so a lamp looks lit rather than like a hole in the shadow.
The lift's glow was a green blob covering the pad. Reach and strength cut by half.
A room of one repeated plate read as wallpaper; every seventh tile, chosen from its own coordinates, is the worn variant now.
The floor-plan guard rejected a perfectly good room for 'one shape covered the whole canvas'. A floor plan is supposed to cover the canvas; that rule is for sprites only.
A plan naming only tiles the library does not have raised out of the rasteriser before the guard could explain why. It reports the problem now.
Two patches failed silently partway through because black had reflowed the lines I was matching on. Both were re-applied against the real text.
not_done_yet: The crew are upscaled, not redrawn: EPX smooths them but does not add detail a 16px sprite never had.
Props do not block movement, still.
Structures can be generated and saved but no game reads them yet — Janhollow does not stamp one into a deck.
The sprite results are crude. The 9B draws better and takes roughly twice as long; it is one choice in the Jan panel.
